sources.what_it_gives: For every course: course ID, title, units, and one description paragraph. Prerequisites, restrictions, credit exclusions, cross-listings, 'Recommended preparation' and 'Formerly/Renumbered from' all sit inside that paragraph as prose. Live counts of p.course-name: DSC 84, MATH 224, CSE 212, PHYS 141, BIOL 247 (one page covers BILD/BICD/BIBC/BIEB/BIMM/BIPN), CHEM 170, COGS 134, ECE 204. It does NOT say which quarters a course is offered. The only offering hints are free text such as 'offered every year' (CHEM, 19 times), 'offered in alternate years' (PHYS) and 'Offered as faculty resources permit' (CSE).
sources.format: Static HTML (Apache, served as text/html UTF-8; DSC page is about 96 KB). No JSON, no API, no per-course URLs. Every course has an anchor (#dsc40a). The site offers no PDF version of the course pages (/pdf/DSC.pdf returned 404).
sources.robots_terms: https://catalog.ucsd.edu/robots.txt returns HTTP 404, so no robots rules are published for this host. Each page has the meta tag `<meta content="index,follow,noarchive" name="robots"/>`. The parent host's https://ucsd.edu/robots.txt has `Disallow: /catalog/`, but that covers the ucsd.edu/catalog/ path, not the catalog.ucsd.edu host. The site-wide Terms of Use (https://ucsd.edu/about/terms-of-use.html, linked from every catalog page footer) say, quoted from the page: 'No material from any official UC San Diego website may be copied, reproduced, republished, ... without explicit permission, except that you may download one copy ... for your personal, non-commercial home use only'. A public Streamlit app that republishes description text goes beyond that clause, so permission should be sought, or the app should store only derived facts (IDs, units, parsed prerequisite edges) and link to the catalog.
sources.freshness: The page header and the disclaimer name the edition: 'UC San Diego General Catalog 2026–27', and the homepage says '2026-27 Catalog Interim Update: Fall'. Every page fetched on 2026-11-12, including the archived 2025-26 pages, had Last-Modified on 2026-11-04 (about 18:09 to 18:31 GMT). That means the whole site is republished in one batch, so Last-Modified does not show whether a page's content changed. ETag is supported: a conditional GET with If-None-Match returned 304. The cadence is inferred, not confirmed: one official edition per year, plus term-labelled 'Interim Update' releases (Fall seen).

found.recommendation:
Use catalog.ucsd.edu as the source of truth for course existence, IDs, titles, units and prerequisite prose, and for the DS major's required core lists. Do NOT use it for quarter offerings: it has no term data beyond occasional prose like 'offered every year' or 'alternate years', so offerings must come from the department projected-offerings pages and the Schedule of Classes. Implementation for a GitHub Actions cron (weekly is ample, since content changes per interim update, i.e. per term): (1) Discover department pages from front/courses.html and fetch only the ~8 needed course pages plus curric/DSC-ug.html. Use conditional GET with a stored ETag (304 verified), a descriptive User-Agent, and at least 1 s between requests. (2) Parse with a sibling-based pairing, not the index-zip in scraper.py: for each p.course-name, take the next non-anchor `

`. Strip the trailing `Tag:…`, read units from the last parenthesised group (handle ranges, 'or' and 4-4-4), and split prerequisites with a regex on text. (3) Normalize IDs: add an alias table for the '/R' suffix (DSC 10 = DSC 10/R) and expand implied subjects ('DSC 20/R and 40A/R'). (4) Store a hash of each course's normalized text and open a PR (not an auto-commit) when anything changes, so prereq_overrides.json and the graph tests are re-reviewed before deploy. (5) Record the edition string from p.course-disclaimer plus the interim-update label in the data file. Optionally load /archive/{year}/ snapshots to support a student's catalog-year requirements. (6) Parse the major requirements partly automatically: the lower-division and core `

  • ` lists can be parsed into AND-of-OR groups, but keep the elective and subject-domain rules hand-curated and alarm when the section's HTML hash changes. (7) Mind the Terms of Use: copying or republishing catalog text needs explicit permission beyond personal non-commercial use. The public app should therefore store derived structured data and link back to the catalog anchor (e.g. courses/DSC.html#dsc40a) rather than redisplaying full descriptions, or the owner should ask the Registrar for permission. The existing dataset already stores full descriptions.

verdict.corrected_recommendation:
Use catalog.ucsd.edu as the source of truth for course existence, IDs, titles, units and prerequisite text. Do not use it for quarter offerings; those must come from the department projected-offerings pages and the Schedule of Classes. Suggested implementation as a weekly GitHub Actions job: (1) Fetch front/courses.html to discover pages. Then fetch only the needed courses/{DSC,MATH,CSE,PHYS,BIOL,CHEM,COGS,ECE}.html and curric/DSC-ug.html. Send a descriptive User-Agent, wait at least 1 s between requests, and send If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since (both return 304). Because the whole site was republished in one batch on 2026-11-04, decide whether anything changed by hashing each course's normalized text, not by Last-Modified. (2) Parse by walking siblings: after each p.course-name, skip p.anchor-parent and take the next

, whatever its class. Do not zip the two lists by index; scraper.py does this and mis-assigns every DSC description from 40B/R on today. Drop the trailing 'Tag:' strong element (55 on CSE). Read units from the last parenthesised group and handle the forms N–N, N or N, N-N-N, 'N to N' and comma lists. Find the prerequisite clause with a text regex (/Prerequisites?\s*:/) over get_text(), not with tag selectors. Separate course edges from non-course conditions (standing, GPA, consent, major restrictions). Get the course level from the course number, because Graduate and BIOL subject headings are h3, not h2. Do not key on anchor ids, since 'dsc40r' is duplicated. (3) Normalize IDs: map 'X/R' to the base ID, expand implied subjects and hyphen sequences ('20/R and 40A/R', '40A/R-B/R', '181A-B-C'), and accept both suffixed and unsuffixed forms in the same text. (4) Version requirements by catalog year. Parse the frozen record (archive/{YYYY-YY}/curric/DSC-ug.html and archive/{YYYY-YY}/courses/*.html, available from 2021-22 on) for each student's catalog year. Store the live interim page as a separate 'interim' layer and show its differences as advisory; the archive page calls interim updates 'for information and advising purposes only'. Today this matters concretely: the DS core changed from 'MATH 189' to 'MATH 189 or DSC 152', and the DSC 180A prerequisite gained '(MATH 189 or DSC 152)'. DSC 152 has no catalog entry yet, so the validator needs a rule for referenced-but-undefined courses (accept them as satisfiable, or flag them). (5) Parse the lower-division and core

  • lists automatically into AND-of-OR groups, allowing for an inline 'or' and a wrapper. Keep the subject-domain and elective rules hand-curated, with an alert when the hash of that section changes. (6) When the parse changes, open a PR rather than committing directly, so prereq_overrides.json and the graph tests are reviewed, and include a per-course diff of prerequisite edges, not only text. Record the edition string from p.course-disclaimer and the 'Catalog Interim Update: ' label from index.html. (7) Licensing: the ucsd.edu Terms of Use forbid reproducing the material, including use 'on any other website or networked computer environment', without explicit permission. The public app should store only derived structured facts (IDs, units, parsed edges) and link to courses/X.html#anchor, or the owner should ask for permission through the ITS contact named in the Terms. The existing dataset already stores full descriptions, so it should be reviewed against this. (8) Do not depend on the catalog PDF links (they 404) or on pre-2021 archives (they redirect to the registrar homepage).

found.recommendation:
1. Treat the live Schedule of Classes as unavailable to the tutor from Fall 2026 on. UCSD moved it to the Triton Student System (TSS), an SAP Fiori app behind SAML SSO at tss.ucsd.edu. UCSD also says it deliberately limited TSS against automated scraping. Do not log in, reuse cookies, or scrape TSS from GitHub Actions or Streamlit.

2. Use the legacy act.ucsd.edu Schedule of Classes as a one-time history of past offerings, not as a live feed. It is public, robots.txt does not block /scheduleOfClasses/, and it holds terms FA24 through SA26.
   - Backfill with POST scheduleOfClassesStudentResult.htm (tabNum=tabs-sub, selectedSubjects=DSC/MATH/CSE/PHYS/BIOL/CHEM/COGS/ECE, schedOption1, 2 and 3 as needed). Then GET scheduleOfClassesStudentResultPrint.htm with the same cookie jar to get every page at once.
   - That is about 2 requests per subject per term. For about 7 regular quarters (FA24, WI25, SP25, FA25, WI26, SP26, plus summers if wanted), it comes to roughly 100-150 requests at 1 request per second.
   - Save a compact offerings_history.json: {course_id: [terms offered], sections, instructors}. The planner can derive 'usually offered in FA/WI/SP' from it to soft-check quarter placement.
   - Optionally also fetch scheduleOfClassesPreReq.htm per course and term to cross-check prereq_overrides.json.
   - Before calling a new term, check subject-list.json?selectedTerm=XXNN. An empty [] means no data.
   - There is no point running this on a schedule: no new terms will appear. A rare manual workflow_dispatch is enough.

3. For FA26 and later offerings, use the other source families: department projected or tentative course-offering pages, and the catalog. Optionally the owner can type the WI27 term in from TSS by hand. Use the Blink enrollment calendar, which is public, to know when a new term's schedule is published (WI27: 11/5/2026; SP27: TBD).

4. If live data is truly needed, the sanctioned route is to ask the registrar or ESR (tss@ucsd.edu, esr-student@ucsd.edu) whether a data feed exists.

5. Licensing: UCSD's terms of use allow personal, non-commercial copies only, and republishing needs explicit permission. A public Streamlit app showing derived 'offered in quarter X' facts is a grey area. Store derived facts only, not raw pages, and link to the official source.
open_questions: Does TSS have any public guest or unauthenticated Schedule of Classes view or export, or an OData endpoint UCSD permits for students? Not verified: unauthenticated access redirects to SAML SSO, and I did not probe further.
Will the legacy act.ucsd.edu Schedule of Classes stay online, and for how long? It still serves FA24-SA26 today but gets no new terms. WI27 even returns HTTP 500 from subject-list.json.
Are the legacy 'As of' timestamps (SP26 stamped 10/12/2026, after the term ended) final snapshots? Do seat counts there reflect end-of-term enrollment? Not verified.
Does api.ucsd.edu (WSO2) offer any course or schedule API to students? Listing APIs requires authentication (401).
Does UCSD's terms of use allow a public Streamlit app to show offering patterns derived from the SoC? Explicit permission may be needed. Ask the Registrar.
Exactly why the GET form of the result URL failed is unknown. It timed out after 40 s with 0 bytes, so treat POST as the only working method.
How the legacy prerequisite page shows OR alternatives (e.g. 'MATH 18 or MATH 31AH') is not verified. I only checked DSC80, which is a plain AND list.

verdict.corrected_recommendation:
1. Live source for current and next term: use the official UCSD Class Planner public API (classplanner.apps.ucsd.edu), not TSS. The legacy system and TSS do not provide this.
   - Run a GitHub Actions cron about once a day. It calls GET /api/v1/public/catalog/terms (1 request) and compares term_code and last_full_refresh_at with the last saved snapshot.
   - When a term is new or has been refreshed, POST /api/v1/public/catalog/courses/search per subject. Use {term_code, subject_code:[S], limit:48, offset} for the 8 subjects in the dataset (DSC, MATH, CSE, PHYS, BIOL, CHEM, COGS, ECE). That is about 15-25 requests at 1 request per second, with the descriptive User-Agent.
   - Normalize codes ('040A' to 'DSC 40A'). Store only derived facts per course: terms offered, units, the prerequisites[] strings and restrictions. Commit them as offerings.json, with source URL and refresh time. Do not store raw responses or instructor and seat data.
   - Do not overwrite prereq_overrides.json automatically. Diff the prerequisites against the parsed catalog graph and open a PR or issue so a person can review it, since R-variants and 'minimum grade D' need handling.
   - Validate the response schema (keys term_code, total, offset, courses[].module_code, prerequisites, sections). If it fails, keep the last good snapshot and fail the workflow loudly, because the API is undocumented.
   - Use only the /api/v1/public/* endpoints. Never use the signed-in /api/v1/catalog, /planner or /user-state endpoints. Never use TSS (SSO, and UCSD explicitly designed it against scraping).

2. History: do a one-time manual backfill from legacy act.ucsd.edu for FA24-SA26, using a workflow_dispatch workflow.
   - A plain GET to scheduleOfClassesStudentResult.htm?selectedTerm=..&tabNum=tabs-sub&selectedSubjects=..&schedOption1=true&schedOption2=true works. So does a POST. For every page at once, use the print view (scheduleOfClassesStudentResultPrint.htm) with the session cookie.
   - Parse the leading 'R' column and the colspan=2 room cell correctly. Use timeouts and retries.
   - From the combined history, derive 'typically offered in FA/WI/SP' as a soft constraint for the planner.

3. Use the Blink calendar (public; robots allows /instructors/) only to know when to expect the next term, e.g. SP27 'TBD'. Drop the struck-through dates. The daily terms check above already detects new terms directly.

4. Licensing: classplanner and act.ucsd.edu are both under ucsd.edu terms of use (personal, non-commercial, no republishing without explicit permission). For a public Streamlit app, show derived offering facts with a link to the official Class Planner or TSS, and say the data may be stale (refresh dates). Email the Registrar or the Class Planner team (via tss@ucsd.edu / ESR) to ask permission and whether a sanctioned feed exists.

verdict.corrected_recommendation:
Most of the overall approach holds: one adapter per department, a weekly GitHub Actions cron, normalized {course_id, academic_year, quarters, status, source_url, fetched_at, content_hash} records, and a validator that treats out-of-year quarters as 'unknown'. The corrections are below.

1. Automate (verified public, robots-allowed):
- CSE CSV. Expect 92 rows, not 105. Follow the 307 redirect and assert the header matches /Course #,Title,(Fall|Winter|Spring) \d{4}/ before writing.
- COGS CSV. gid=866922720 only. No duplicate-row handling is needed, but collapse 'A00'/'B00' section rows into one course.
- MATH HTML. The 6/4-td rowspan parse reproduces 172 courses.
- DSC TablePress. Use the WP REST 'modified' only as a hint and always hash the table.
- PHYS offerings, plus the frequency page at its new URL /typical-course-frequencies-terms. Take headers from <thead> only.
- ECE. Parse by column position and key on the catalog href fragment (#ece101). Strip zero-padding and the <style> blocks (9 of them, not one per row).
- Optionally ECON (server-rendered table) if domain electives are added.

2. Manual or ask first:
- CHEM: robots 'Disallow: /ext/'. Do not automate; hand-enter CHEM 6A/6B/6C/11 yearly.
- BIOL (BILD/BIBC): the backup JSON is not robots-blocked (correcting the researcher), but its shape is UNVERIFIED and the APIs are undocumented. Ask the School of Biological Sciences before automating, and hand-enter the 5 courses until then.

3. Semantics:
- Absent from a list means 'not listed', not 'not offered'. Special-case DSC 197/198/199 as by-arrangement. Treat MATH 182-style year alternation with a labelled previous-year guess or the PHYS-style frequency.
- Prefer each table over the DSC FAQ prose.
- Ingest the PHYS Pilot Prereqs notice into the prereq review queue.

4. Ground truth: the legacy act.ucsd.edu Schedule of Classes stops at SU26. FA26 onward is in TSS, whose public access is UNVERIFIED and must be checked separately before it is used as the cross-check.

5. Terms and privacy:
- Store only course-quarter booleans and never instructor names.
- Never fetch the COGS staffing tabs.
- Rate-limit to 1 request per second or slower with the descriptive User-Agent.
- Because the UCSD ToU explicitly prohibits use 'on any other website', email the departments (or the registrar) for permission before the public Streamlit app shows this data. Until then, show only derived availability flags with source links and a 'tentative, check TSS' banner.

found.recommendation:
UCSD has no official public course, catalog, term or schedule API a student can just use. The API gateway at api.ucsd.edu requires a UCSD SSO account, and each API needs its own approval, which can take days. Anonymous browsing of its API list is off, and I found no public evidence that a course or schedule API exists there. The live Schedule of Classes now sits inside TSS (SAP), which requires login. UCSD's new Class Planner JSON API (classplanner.apps.ucsd.edu) was reportedly open before but now returns 401 'Sign in to continue'. Do not build on SSO-gated or undocumented endpoints, and do not put a personal session cookie into Streamlit or CI.

Suggested plan:
1. Catalog and prerequisites: keep scraping catalog.ucsd.edu/courses/<DEPT>.html, which is public static HTML. Another source family covers this.
2. Offering history: import the MIT-licensed historical Schedule of Classes TOMLs (WI95–SU26) once, and compute for each course which quarters it was offered over the last N years.
3. Current quarters (FA26 onward): consume alchin2/tssplusplus data/offered/<term>.csv (MIT, refreshed on Blink publication dates). Pin the commit SHA and treat it as unofficial, best-effort data. The fallback is department projected-offerings pages.
4. Refresh triggers: a scheduled GitHub Actions job that parses the public Blink 'Schedule of Classes: Publication Schedule' table, re-pulls new term data, opens a PR with a diff, and runs the validator tests before merge.
5. Requirements and evaluation: use the public plans.ucsd.edu controller.php JSON (major code DS25; 2025 plans exist, 2026 not yet published) as reference sequences.
6. Official access: if the owner wants an official API, they can log in to api.ucsd.edu with their own SSO to see whether any course or term API is listed, or email ITS. They can also ask ITS (crose@ucsd.edu) for permission to republish catalog content on the public Streamlit app.

verdict.corrected_recommendation:
The core conclusion holds: UCSD has no official public API for courses, the catalog, terms or the Schedule of Classes. api.ucsd.edu, TSS (sis/tss.ucsd.edu) and the Class Planner API (now 401 'Sign in to continue') all need SSO. Never put a personal session cookie into Streamlit or CI. Corrected plan for the tutor:
1. Catalog and prerequisites: keep scraping the public static https://catalog.ucsd.edu/courses/<DEPT>.html at 1 request/second or slower. The TSS impact doc lists the General Catalog as 'Staying'. Harden the parser for <strong>/<em> variants, using CuteSurtr/prereq-dependency (MIT) as a cross-check. Note in the UI that TSS enforces CourseLeaf enrollment requirements that may differ from catalog prose.
2. Offering history: import the MIT SheepTester-forks historical TOMLs (WI95–SU26) once and compute per-course quarter frequency. Before the legacy act.ucsd.edu Schedule of Classes retires in mid-December 2026, manually spot-check a few DSC/MATH terms against it. It is public and responds today; do this as a person through the page, not as an automated form-posting scraper.
3. FA26 onward: treat alchin2/tssplusplus data/offered/<term>.csv as an optional, unofficial signal. Pin it to a commit SHA, filter out graduate and non-major courses, expect gaps for spring and summer, and show it as 'reported offered', never as a hard validator constraint. Department tentative-offering pages are the main forward-looking source. CSE's page is live; DSC and MATH pages still need to be found.
4. Refresh: a scheduled GitHub Actions job that parses the Blink publication table (normalize 'E.Schedule' vs 'E. Schedule', strip '*', handle 'TBA'). On a new date it re-pulls the sources above, opens a PR with a diff, and runs the validator tests. Use GITHUB_TOKEN or raw.githubusercontent.com to avoid GitHub API rate limits.
5. Requirements and evaluation: use the public plans.ucsd.edu controller.php JSON with DS25 and year 2025. The site says majors without a 2026-27 plan had no substantial changes, so the 2025 plan is current.
6. Compliance and official access: store structured facts (codes, units, prerequisite edges, terms offered) plus links rather than verbatim catalog descriptions on the public app, or ask ITS (crose@ucsd.edu) for permission. If the owner wants an official API, they must log in to api.ucsd.edu with their own SSO, or contact ITS. Neither I nor the original researcher could see the API list.

found.recommendation:
How the planner should use these sources:

1. Allowed and appropriate for a scheduled GitHub Action, each with low-rate GETs using the UA 'ucsd-course-planning-tutor (student project)', at most 1 request per second, and a robots.txt check at runtime:
   - blink academic calendar HTML (calendars/{year}.html), to get quarter dates. Do not fetch the robots-disallowed .ics or PDF.
   - blink booking/registration calendar, to schedule the Schedule of Classes refresh.
   - The DSC WordPress pages: major and minor requirements, course offerings, petitions, advising.
   - catalog.ucsd.edu/curric/DSC-ug.html.
   - Sparingly, plans.ucsd.edu controller.php JSON, for sample plans and evals.

2. Use the DSC site's WP REST API as a cheap change detector: /wp-json/wp/v2/pages?slug=...&_fields=slug,modified. Re-parse only when 'modified' changes. Route requirement changes to a pull request for human review rather than auto-merging, because the requirements are prose with alternatives and footnotes.

3. Store extracted facts (codes, units, prerequisite edges, quarters, dates) plus source URLs and fetch timestamps. Avoid republishing verbatim catalog or department prose in the public Streamlit app: the UCSD Terms of Use prohibit copying or republishing material from official sites without explicit permission. If full descriptions are needed, email ITS (crose@ucsd.edu, the contact listed in the Terms) for permission.

4. Do not automate CAPE results, SET reports or DARS:
   - All three redirect to a5.ucsd.edu tritON SSO.
   - SET's own page says its data is 'not intended for project or research use' without approval.
   - PPM 135-9 Appendix A #4 and #7 cover circumventing access processes and copying University data.
   - Keep these as outbound links only, and fix the app's CAPE deep link to point to set.ucsd.edu. If evaluation data is wanted, the route is an instructor-filed SET data request.

5. Also fix the two dead links in app.py (datascience.ucsd.edu /current-students/course-information/ and /current-students/advising/ both return 404). Replace them with /current-students/major-requirements/ and /current-students/academic-advising/.
open_questions: Does UCSD (ITS or the catalog office) consider extracting facts from catalog and department pages for a public student app acceptable without permission, or is only linking acceptable? The Terms of Use text is broad, and its 'one personal copy' exception does not cover a deployed app. Needs a direct email to the Terms' permissions contact (crose@ucsd.edu).
PPM 135-9's 'Next Review Date: 10/03/2025' has passed and the compliancebridge copy shows no revision. Unverified whether a newer version exists.

The academic calendar .ics (/_files/SCI-tab/2026-2027-academic-calendar.ics) and the printer-friendly PDF were not fetched because blink robots.txt disallows /_files and *.pdf. Their contents are UNVERIFIED.
plans.ucsd.edu controller.php is an undocumented internal endpoint. Acceptable request volume and stability are unknown, and the 2026 DSC plan is not yet published (major_code 'NONE').

There is no dedicated DSC 'requirement changes' or changelog page; changes are visible only as page-modified timestamps. Whether HDSI announces changes elsewhere (for example the 'DSC Newsletter Site' mentioned on the advising page) is not verified.

Whether the Schedule of Classes (act.ucsd.edu/scheduleOfClasses) permits automated querying beyond robots.txt (which disallows only /cwp/tools/search) is covered by another source family and was not examined here.

verdict.corrected_recommendation:
The finding is mostly accurate. Its main errors are the robots-parsing advice, the missed strikethrough dates in the enrollment calendar, and the slug collision in the REST watcher. Corrected plan:

1. Polite fetching. Set the UA to 'ucsd-course-planning-tutor (student project)', wait at least 1 second between requests, and cache responses.
   - Do not rely on urllib.robotparser, because it ignores wildcards and would allow blink's 'Disallow: *.pdf'. Use protego, or a hard-coded denylist: blink /_files and /search, any *.pdf, *.xls, *.doc or *.ics, and act /cwp/tools/search.
   - Never touch SSO-gated hosts: CAPE Results.aspx, academicaffairs SET, act DARS, or anything that redirects to a5.ucsd.edu. If a 302 to a5.ucsd.edu ever appears, treat it as a stop signal.

2. Scheduled GitHub Action sources, in order of value:
   a. DSC course-offerings TablePress table (#tablepress-4, columns Course # | Title | Quarter). Normalize 'DSC-040A' to 'DSC 40A', strip suffixes such as '(1 IWC)', split 'DSC-190/291', drop 5xx graduate rows, and treat the result as tentative. The Schedule of Classes overrides it once published.
   b. The blink enrollment calendar. Remove <span style="text-decoration: line-through;"> values first. Use the 'Schedule of Classes and Booking times available' date to trigger the Schedule of Classes refresh.
